exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong weather investigation lets the box plot do the talking — here is how one student compared rainfall in two towns.

traits.trait: Reads the box plot's five numbers
traits.sample: My box plot shows min 0 mm, Q1 2 mm, median 6 mm, Q3 11 mm, max 20 mm — half of all days got between 2 and 11 mm.
traits.why: All five summary numbers are stated with what they mean.

traits.sample: Town A's IQR of 9 mm versus Town B's 3 mm means Town B's rainfall is far more predictable.
traits.why: IQR is turned into a claim about real weather, not left as a number.

traits.trait: Chooses the display for a reason
traits.sample: I chose a box plot over a dot plot because with 30 days of data, the box shows the spread at a glance.
traits.why: The display choice is justified by the data's size and the question.

traits.sample: One 45 mm storm raised the mean by 1.3 mm but left the median alone, so I reported the median as the typical day.
traits.why: The reliable measure is picked because of the outlier evidence.
